questions.question: What is electric current?
choices: The rate of electric charge flow
The amount of energy stored in every battery
The resistance of a wire divided by time

questions.question: What is voltage?
choices: The number of electrons in an atom
Electric potential difference between two points

questions.question: What is electrical resistance?
choices: The total mass of a circuit
The distance between a switch and a lamp

questions.question: Which unit measures current?
Which unit measures resistance?
What is a series circuit?
choices: A circuit with one path through its components
A circuit that has no power source
A circuit with several independent branches
A circuit in which current never flows

questions.question: What is a parallel circuit?
choices: A circuit containing more than one branch for current
A circuit with all components on one path

questions.question: Why does opening a simple series switch stop current?
choices: The battery loses all stored charge instantly
Every wire becomes a magnet permanently

questions.question: Why are metals often used as conducting wires?
choices: Their nuclei travel around the whole circuit
Their electrons all remain fixed in place
They contain charges that can move through the material

questions.question: For an ohmic resistor at constant temperature, what happens to current if voltage doubles?
For a fixed voltage, what happens to current when resistance increases?
choices: It increases in the same proportion
It becomes independent of the source

questions.question: Why can one lamp go out while another stays lit in separate parallel branches?
choices: An intact branch can retain its own complete path
Both branches must have identical current at every moment
A broken lamp creates a new battery

questions.question: What role does a battery play in a simple circuit?
choices: It removes all resistance from the wires
It creates electrons from nothing whenever needed
It uses chemical processes to maintain a potential difference

questions.question: How should an ammeter be connected to measure current through a component?
choices: Across the component without entering its path
Across the battery terminals as a short circuit

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure a component's potential difference?
choices: Instead of the battery in the only current path
In series as the only conducting route
Only at one point without another connection

questions.question: A 6 V source is connected to a 3 Ω ohmic resistor. Using I = V/R, what current flows?
Two resistors of 2 Ω and 4 Ω are connected in series. What is their total resistance?
A lamp draws 2 A at 12 V. Using P = VI, what power does it use?
Two identical resistors are connected in parallel instead of using one alone. What happens to the equivalent resistance?
choices: It stays equal to one resistor
It becomes the sum of both resistances
It becomes half the resistance of one

questions.question: A circuit draws more current than its rated protective fuse permits. What is the fuse designed to do?
choices: Break the circuit to reduce the risk of overheating
Lower the wire's resistance to zero
